findings.title: No line-level slips found in the changed hunks
findings.description:
I read each changed hunk for the listed slip types and found none. In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the match counter and timestamp are updated and the return value is the block check, which is the intended behavior. In `EmailValidator#validate_each`, the `attribute` and `value` arguments are used consistently, and the blocked check is guarded by `errors[attribute].blank?` as intended. In `users_controller.rb`, `errors.to_hash` and `attributes.slice(...)` are standard ActiveRecord calls. In `create_account_controller.js`, `rejectedEmails` is initialized with `Em.A([])`, and the `contains` and `pushObject` calls match the array API. The spec names match the behavior they exercise: the "doesn't add an error" and "adds an error" examples, and the `:block` and `:do_nothing` contexts. The `EmailValidator` spec's `described_class.new({attributes: :email})` call is well formed.

This review is limited to the diff. I did not open the surrounding files, so I make no claim about callers outside the hunks, such as any remaining uses of the removed `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`.

structured_findings.summary: No line-level slips found in the changed hunks
